What video game cliche drives you nuts?

This stemmed from a discussion we're having in work about Destiny, how pretty much every mission is "Hold them off while I open this door/hack this terminal."

So yeah, that's a big one for me...
Enemies that endlessly spawn until you perform some menial task... like, "We got the whole army behind us!" "Wait, he got the Intel? Fuck it, guys, let's leave..."
Getting knocked out by one mook in a cutscene when i've been unstoppable for the whole rest of the game.

For me it's the opposite of that, when the character suddenly becomes far more badass and capable in a cutscene than when I'm in control. Really breaks the immersion for me.

Doubly so in games like RE5 when chris or whomever fires a gun in the cutscenes. Like, bitch don't use my bullets!

or even how chris and shiva move in cutscenes. Barrel rolling into an epic crouch pose, running and gunning, taking out everything in one shot. Then you're put back in control and 'oh god no why do i keep getting killed by bats.'
This million times this. The worst example of this happening to me was in Mass Effect 3 whenever that chucklefuck space ninja Kai Leng shows up in a cut scene everyone else turns into a retard.
ME3 flashbacks, shudder why do they Never use shields/techs/biotics in cutscenes?
When the final boss is really easy.
Open-world games with "THE CHOSEN ONE" tainted storylines. I want to play a game where you're a part of a living world, not some theme park adventure.

I'm getting pretty tired of marathon waves of mooks in lieu of bosses. It's boring, grind-y and unsatisfying.

Give us an actual boss fight dammit.
Everything in the game being colored a shade of brown.

Game play mechanics or story? If we are talking about story... -The Hero with amnesia -The Hero's home town burning down -The slightly younger spunky side kick -The guy you thought was the bad guy for most of the game is actually just a puppet
Escort missions, especially when the idiot AI runs out in front of everyone and gets shot, and somehow it's my fault.
Everything in the universe stops until you do one stupid thing.
Having to knock out the boss 3 times (every nintendo game ever)
When a game tries to be hard just to be hard and for no other reason. Difficulty jumps that start way to late come as a close second.
Especially if they step over that fine line between being difficult/challenging and just being plain frustrating.
I hate that so much, happens way to often in the Japanese super mario bros 2.

Recently I bought AVGN Adventure, which I really think manages that balance so well. It's like a classic sidescroller and the stages are very difficult, but there are lots of savepoints to spare your blood pressure and it's fun, so instead of annoying you, every time you die you get eager to try again. It's great, I really recommend it.
I have always kind have assumed that game was like Bunny Must Die/Chelsea and the Seven Devils and you would need some downtime to play it.

I don't know that one, but AVGN Adventure it a 16 bit style sidescroller with 8 stages and a final boss stage. The stages themselves aren't super long, but they are very challenging and fun to play. If you are interested, on the Cinemassacre/Angry Video Game Nerd Youtube channel, he has an episode where he talks about AVGN inspired games and this one is the last and largest mentioned in the video. I really love it, got it at the recent Steam sale and it definitely was worth buying.

Link to Steam, where it has very positive reviews.
